0x04e82.name: walk the player state with a table and a handler
0x04e82.why: the table at 0x1f5f0 and the routine at 0xc8de, with the record at 0x3e0e7e - a pairing this file uses nowhere else.

0x0522e.name: turn the current player's record into a table offset
0x0522e.why: follows 0x3e1960 to the current player, takes the pointer at 0x42 and hands it to offsetRecordTableBase with the table at 0x1fae4.

0x05d8c.name: halt the machine unless the level argument is above seven
0x05d8c.why: subtracts seven and returns without doing anything if the result is not positive; the 68000's interrupt levels stop at seven, so this is the guard on an out-of-range one.

0x06154.name: draw the cell's owner, then step to the previous row
0x06154.why: one call to cellOwnerDraw with a one, then the backwards row step - the only case in this walk that draws.

0x064c8.name: drop the pushed word and step to the next row
0x064c8.why: the return path for the cases that pushed a single coordinate.

0x0704e.name: step the flier's position and age it
0x0704e.why: gives up when the sprite pointer at 0x16(a2) is null; otherwise it counts the frame and adds the velocity words at 6 and 0xa into the 16.6 fixed-point position.

0x09d8c.name: set the timer to fifteen and draw two lines
0x09d8c.why: phaseTimerSet with 0xf and two calls to textLineDraw - the pair that holds an award on screen.

0x18b92.name: decompress a tile straight to a screen address
0x18b92.why: adds the offset to 0x200004 itself rather than taking a coordinate, which is what separates it from the entry that builds the address from a row and a column.

0x1ad46.name: take the sign-extended value off word 0x1c and mark it changed
0x1ad46.why: the arithmetic and then `ori.b #1,(a4)` - the driver's change byte - where the entry above it does the same without the mark.

0x061bc.name: drop the pushed word and step to the previous row
0x061bc.why: the return path for the cases here that pushed a single coordinate.

0x066fa.name: stop when the column reaches forty-two
0x066fa.why: 0x2a is the board's 42 columns; reaching it falls into the restore and rts.

0x09e96.name: draw the queue gate word as a line of text
0x09e96.why: reads the word at 0x3e1948 - the gate the cue queue is switched by - and hands it to textLineDraw, which is the only thing this entry does.

0x0ac4c.name: pick a random value for the station the byte at 0x3e195c names
0x0ac4c.why: keeps two records, 0x3e1caa and 0x3e1cb2, and indexes with the station byte before drawing on the generator.

0x0cbe8.name: skip a player whose status bit is clear or whose byte 0x1d is set
0x0cbe8.why: the two guards every walk over the player array uses: the top bit of the status word at (a3), and the byte at 0x1d.

0x0cc36.name: drop the pushed argument and go on to the parity check
0x0cc36.why: the return path for the case that queued a cue; it rejoins at the even-parity branch.

0x0d048.name: drop eight pushed bytes and wait
0x0d048.why: the return path for the case above it, which pushed two longs.

0x0d45c.name: wait on the event at 0x11b1e
0x0d45c.why: the tail every battle phase reaches: it asks eventTest for that record and branches on whether the answer is zero.

0x0dad6.name: draw the rectangle at a fixed screen place
0x0dad6.why: 0xf0, 2 and 0x12 pushed as the constants, and the screen base 0x200004 with 0x60 added - so where it draws is not an argument at all.

0x11f08.name: start from an offset already in hand rather than a tile id
0x11f08.why: reads its offset straight out of the frame and adds it to the tile base, where the entry above looks the id up in a table first.

0x1232a.name: jump to whichever decoder state a4 holds
0x1232a.why: one instruction: `jmp (a4)`. The state machine's whole dispatch, which is why the address registers had to hold code before it could be judged against silicon.

0x124e4.name: read the next control byte and branch on its top bit
0x124e4.why: a negative byte takes the run path with the low five bits as its length; a positive one is a literal.

0x125f8.name: drop this entry's countdown and run it when it reaches zero
0x125f8.why: byte 0xe is the countdown and byte 0xd the reload; when it expires the record's pointer at 8 becomes the palette RAM address the handler works on.

0x12350.name: store d4 through a1 and return
0x12350.why: two instructions, and no state pointer is moved - the emit that does not advance the decoder.

0x130dc.name: pack the failing address beside the pattern and unmask
0x130dc.why: swaps the pattern into the high half and puts the address register's low word beside it, then drops the interrupt mask to 0x2000.

0x154a8.name: draw the text at a fixed attribute with the byte at 0x3e3d7b
0x154a8.why: 0x2040 is the attribute pushed, and the signed byte at 0x3e3d7b is the second half of the pair the tail stores.

0x15562.name: measure the string at 0x1dfb2 with the default attributes
0x15562.why: every argument is a constant - 0x2040, the string, 0x1b and 0xffff - so this wrapper is entirely its argument list.

0x15598.name: call the sound table initialiser and return
0x15598.why: a jsr and an rts, which is the whole routine.

0x16d48.name: drop the pushed argument and go to the shared tail
0x16d48.why: the return path for the reset case above it.

0x1886a.name: decompress this slot's tiles, then finish the loop
0x1886a.why: one call to decompressChainSTilesInto and a branch to the loop end.

0x188c2.name: run the slot's script only when the test byte is zero
0x188c2.why: the slot number times four indexes the pointer table at 0x34(a2), and that pointer is the script it runs.

0x18906.name: restore the saved registers and return

0x196ac.name: read the coin slot state, or answer 0xff
0x196ac.why: 0xff is what it hands back when the word at 0x3e340c says the state at 0x3e3672 cannot be read.

0x1ac98.name: split the operand into its three ranges
0x1ac98.why: 0x16 and above returns at once, under 6 takes one path and the rest another - the bounds that decide which of the three-byte readers runs.

0x1ace4.name: sign-extend into word 0x1c and mark it changed
0x1ace4.why: the store and then the branch into the change-marking tail, where the entry above it stores without marking.

0x1adc4.name: step the script pointer four bytes on
0x1adc4.why: `addq.l #4,$4(a2)` and the jump back - what a test does when it declines to take its branch.

0x1ae24.name: drop eight pushed bytes and go back to the sequencer
0x1ae24.why: the return path for the cases that pushed the record and an operand.

0x16958.name: draw the same cell down a run of rows
0x16958.why: column, first row and count come off the frame and the row counter is seeded from the first - a run down the screen rather than one cell.

0x16c18.name: wait a frame, then read the two values a row needs
0x16c18.why: one call through the wait, then mergeMaskedResultBits twice - with 0x30000f0 and with zero - which is what supplies each row.

0x16fe0.name: draw the service frame for this step
0x16fe0.why: sign-extends the step number and hands it to drawServiceScreenSFrame with a zero.

0x18006.name: store the attribute byte, then the colour word
0x18006.why: byte 0x3e3d7b takes the attribute and the word at 0x22(a7) the colour - the signed pair this tail is named for.

0x190a2.name: draw what the sixteen-byte buffer already holds
0x190a2.why: pushes the buffer at -0x10(a6) with a coordinate assembled out of two of its own argument bytes; the formatting happened in the entry above.

0x1940e.name: clear the band starting at the row the byte names
0x1940e.why: the row byte is swapped and shifted down four - the 0x1000 a cell-row takes - and added to the screen base.

0x197a0.name: take the long path when the divisor will not fit in a word
0x197a0.why: 0x10000 is the test; below it the word divide is enough, at or above it this does the fifteen-step shift-and-subtract.

0x1a3e6.name: walk the channel list keeping both list heads
0x1a3e6.why: 0x3e3d12 and 0x3e3d0e in registers - the two heads the driver moves records between - and the record's byte at 1 decides which.

0x1a618.name: note whether this channel already had a script
0x1a618.why: one test of the long at (a2), and the 0 or 1 it leaves in the frame at -0xa(a6) is what every later branch in the routine reads.

0x1ad4c.name: mark the driver's change byte and go back
0x1ad4c.why: `ori.b #1,(a4)` and the jump - the tail several of the field writers share.

0x1ad66.name: add the value to word 0x1a and go back
0x1ad66.why: the add and the jump, with no sign extension of its own - the caller has already done it.

0x1b062.name: hand the channel record back and return
0x1b062.why: `move.l a2,d0` before the restore, so the routine answers with the record it worked on.

0x1e6e0.name: look the tile id up in the table at 0x2161a
0x1e6e0.why: doubles the id, reads the word and writes it back over the argument's own low half - which is why that slot looks like two different things.

0x0b7fa.name: score the wall runs around a record for the computer player
0x0b7fa.why: 0x14 is the score step it works in, and it walks from field 0x38 of the record; the running total is built by adding and subtracting 0xc and 5 against a frame word before each candidate is compared.

0x0b5e4.name: resolve an owner code against the current record
0x0b5e4.why: keeps the current-record pointer at 0x3e1c84 in a3 and the record at 0x3e1cb0 as a constant, which is the pairing this routine is entirely about.

0x1425c.name: move a sound record between the two driver lists
0x1425c.why: 0x3e352a and 0x3e3508 are the two list bases held in address registers, and 0x3e3536 is the bound the argument is compared against to decide which it belongs to.

0x069e2.name: step across the board in the direction field 0x46 names
0x069e2.why: the two bytes at 0x46 of the record are the direction, copied into the frame before the walk; the kind it lays comes from the word argument.

0x15100.name: find the thirty-byte table entry the index names
0x15100.why: the index times fifteen, doubled, added to the pointer at 0x1d644 - thirty bytes an entry, and the whole routine.

0x0f306.name: allocate an entity from the mask of free slots
0x0f306.why: the count is inverted and shifted down by the index to make a mask of what is still free; the table base is the constant 0x3e0000.

0x0ecfa.name: draw from the chain the record's field 0x4a points at
0x0ecfa.why: 0xc is the step it walks in, and 0x4a of the argument record is the chain head - the only field it reads before the loop.

0x03e84.name: fill the claimed slot and draw its column
0x03e84.why: keeps decompressOneColumnAdvancing's address in a3 and gates the whole thing on the byte at 0x3e0e78.

0x14ef8.name: scale a sound parameter, bounded at six slots
0x14ef8.why: the slot index is compared against 6 - the same bound soundChannelBound uses - before the value and the scale are applied.

0x04760.name: clear the framebuffer band the table at 0xfe0e names
0x04760.why: the word argument indexes 0xfe0e and what it finds is what the band clear is run with.

0x0c568.name: reset the palette effect lists and raise the busy byte
0x0c568.why: writes 0x3e20a0 - the active list head - into 0x3e20a4 so the list is empty, and sets the byte at 0x3e2498 that every effect tick tests first. 0x32 is the number of records it threads.

0x05346.name: resolve the owner through the record's field 0x42
0x05346.why: follows 0x42 of the argument and hands it to the resolver with the table at 0x1fafe.

0x0603e.name: count this cell and read it, walking from the table
0x0603e.why: bumps both tallies on the record - words 0x56 and 0x58 - before it reads the cell, which is how the walk counts what it covered. The address comes from d5, which this half of the family walks.

0x0634a.name: count this cell and read it, walking from the counter
0x0634a.why: bumps both tallies on the record - words 0x56 and 0x58 - before it reads the cell, which is how the walk counts what it covered. The address comes from d4 here rather than d5 - the only difference between the two.

0x071d0.name: take the 0x30 branch, or fall to the plain case
0x071d0.why: one compare against 0x30 and two branches; the entry above it does the same for 0x11.

0x1ad58.name: add the operand to field 0x19
0x1ad58.why: the add and the jump back, without the load of field 0x5d the entry above it does first - so this one adds whatever is already in the register.

0x1ada8.name: store the shifted value back into field 0x5d
0x1ada8.why: the write and the jump back; the shift itself happened in the entry above.

0x043c2.name: walk a table of offsets against a base
0x043c2.why: 0xeb0 and the screen base are the constants; each word the table yields is added to the base argument, and the count is what it answers.

0x05ab0.name: build the piece bag by halving and quartering the count
0x05ab0.why: the count is shifted right one and two straight away, so the bag is filled in those proportions from the two tables it is handed.

0x069ae.name: walk the shot records with their field constants
0x069ae.why: 0x3e0f48 is the base, 0x1a the stride and 0x59 the field it reaches - the three numbers that are the whole routine.

0x19c3c.name: read both trackball axes and record their directions
0x19c3c.why: 0x6c0000 and 0x6c0001 are the two latches, each handed to the direction tracker with its own record at 0x3e367c.

0x05b16.name: drop the player's timer, or reset field 0x24 when it expires
0x05b16.why: byte 0x15 is the countdown and 0xff88 is what field 0x24 takes when it reaches zero.

0x0a7e6.name: read the player state a word and a byte name
0x0a7e6.why: the word at 0xa(a7) and the byte at 0xf(a7) are its two arguments, both zero-extended before the call.

0x18418.name: bump the bookkeeping counter, then start the sequence
0x18418.why: writeBookkeepingCounter with 0x14 first, then the word at 0x284 - a vector-table slot - is what it works from.

0x0ea46.name: clamp the station count to four and set the mode byte to six
0x0ea46.why: 0x3e195c is the station count, pinned at 4, and 0x3e0dd2 - the mode byte drawing and phases branch on - is set to 6.

0x128bc.name: pick a random offset in a range of sixty-four
0x128bc.why: 0x40 is the range handed to rng and 0x60 the bias added to what comes back.

0x046b0.name: fade the palette toward the table at 0x1ee80
0x046b0.why: one call with that table and a one; the whole routine is its argument list.

0x090fe.name: queue the cue byte the argument names
0x090fe.why: the low byte at 7(a7), zero-extended into the ring push at 0x90be - the same ring passByteOnlyWhenGate feeds.

0x0cdc0.name: step the unit and drop what it pushed
0x0cdc0.why: the last routine in the image longer than six bytes without a stated purpose. It sets its arguments up, calls the unit step and cleans the stack - a wrapper whose work is entirely its argument list.
